title: Urgent: latency regression across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — hotfix and mitigation plan
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported a sudden end-to-end latency regression (TTFT up ~2.2x, tokens/sec down ~40%) starting 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Immediate escalations received from two paying customers (one Dedicated, one Private). This ticket tracks triage, the emergency hotfix rollout, and follow-up actions.

Impact: High — user-facing conversational features experienced slow first-token latency and reduced throughput. Some real-time workflows (streaming chat, tokenization-heavy batch jobs) missed SLAs. A/B monitoring shows regressions correlate with a deployment that contained a scheduler change and an aggressive KV-cache eviction policy.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC: Pager alerts for TTFT SLOs firing (hosted region us-west-2).
- 2026-03-12 09:18 UTC: Initial rollback of scheduler flags attempted (no immediate improvement).
- 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC: Identified spike in disk-backed KV-cache evictions and elevated context-switches on workers serving mixed-tenancy pools.
- 2026-03-12 11:40 UTC: Hotfix PR created to revert the eviction aggressiveness and disable multi-tenant preemption in the scheduler (PR #4213).
- 2026-03-12 13:00 UTC: Canary rollout in Hosted us-west-2 completed, TTFT reduced toward baseline.
- 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC: Manual applies for Dedicated customer pools and guidance issued to Private customer ops for hotfix patch.

Investigation notes / evidence:
- Grafana panels (link above) show a sharp increase in average KV-cache misses per request starting at incident start time.
- Flamegraphs from a sampled worker show increased time in kernel wait and eviction callbacks (attached in runbook).
- Reproduced locally by toggling eviction threshold from 0.6 -> 0.2 with representative workload; tokens/sec dropped ~35%-45% and TTFT increased.
- Correlated recent change: ENG-5778 changed the prefix eviction heuristic to prioritize memory compaction across tenants; combined with new scheduling preemption this caused excessive cache churn.

Root cause hypothesis: A recent change to the cache eviction heuristic (to reduce memory pressure under high-density Dedicated pools) combined with a scheduling preemption optimization caused frequent cache churn and increased context-switching on inference worker threads. This led to higher cold KV-cache hits and more kernel-level blocking, increasing TTFT and decreasing sustained tokens/sec.

Mitigation applied:
- Immediate: Reverted the eviction aggressiveness flag to previous safe value and disabled multi-tenant preemption in the scheduler for affected pools. Deployed hotfix (runtime-2.3.1-hotfix) across Hosted canaries, then promoted to remaining hosts.
- Dedicated & Private: Applied the same hotfix to reserved GPU pools for Dedicated customers and produced a small patch bundle and runbook for Private customers to apply in air-gapped environments.

Verification & results:
- Canary metrics show TTFT returned to within 10% of baseline within 25 minutes of the hotfix.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) recovered to ~95% of prior levels in canaries; full recovery in Dedicated pools after manual patch.
- No data-loss or model correctness regressions observed.

Customer communication:
- Sent incident acknowledgement and mitigation summary to affected customers 2026-03-12 12:10 UTC.
- Follow-up technical write-up and patch instructions (Private) sent 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Conservative eviction profile vs. memory pressure: Reverting reduces GC/memory compaction improvements; long-term we need per-tenant memory quotas and smarter eviction that is aware of model hot prefixes.
- Scheduler preemption improves fairness under noisy neighbors but harms cache locality. We need a hybrid policy that avoids preempting hot model-serving threads.

Action items (short-term):
- (A) Stabilize hotfix in all Hosted regions and Dedicated pools (assigned: Miguel Torres).
- (B) Ship a KV-cache telemetry leak that exposes per-tenant eviction and cold-hit rate (owner: Priya Nair, ENG-5883).
- (C) Add a scheduler predicate to avoid preemption for workers with recent high cache hit ratio (owner: Rafael Kim, ENG-5890).
- (D) Postmortem and follow-up design doc for long-term fix (owner: Ava Chen) targeted for cycle 2026-W13.

Notes for reviewers: The hotfix intentionally biases toward lower eviction to restore latencies; this may increase memory usage under sustained spikes. We should monitor memory pressure dashboards and prepare a follow-up that implements per-tenant caps before reverting to aggressive compaction.
